title: Prince William Opens India Visit in a Handloom Jacket Woven in West Bengal
excerpt: The Prince of Wales played gully cricket and drank kulhad chai with Sachin Tendulkar in Mumbai, wearing a custom KARDO waistcoat, as the three-day Earthshot-centred visit got under way.
body:
• Prince William and Kate, the Prince and Princess of Wales, began a three-day India visit in Mumbai on Monday, November 16, opening with gully cricket and kulhad chai at Ballard Estate rather than a Gateway of India photo call.
  • William's deep blue sleeveless jacket was custom-made by Indian label KARDO, from handloom cotton woven using an extra-weft technique by artisans in Harali village, West Bengal.
  • KARDO founder Rikki Kher named the weavers behind the cloth — Netai Mana and Brojokishore Maity — and said he was happiest that their craft was getting recognition.
  • The visit is centred on the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai; the couple travel on to New Delhi to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Prince William opened his India visit not with a staged photograph at the Gateway of India, but with a game of gully cricket, a cup of kulhad chai and a jacket woven on a handloom in West Bengal. The Prince and Princess of Wales arrived in Mumbai on Monday, November 16, for a three-day visit built around the 2026 Earthshot Prize, and their first public appearance — a morning game with school students at Ballard Estate, guided by Sachin Tendulkar — put Indian craft at the centre of the pictures, according to IndulgeExpress and ANI.

The jacket

William wore a deep blue sleeveless, Nehru jacket-style waistcoat over a white shirt with rolled-up sleeves and black trousers. The piece was custom-made by KARDO, the Indian clothing label founded by London-born creative director Rikki Kher, and was crafted from handloom cotton woven using an extra-weft technique by skilled artisans in Harali village, West Bengal, IndulgeExpress reported. ANI's first report of the appearance described the waistcoat as reportedly by KARDO and noted the label had yet to officially confirm it; Kher has since described the making of the piece in detail.

"This fabric is woven on a handloom using an extra weft technique, a process where motifs are laid into the cloth by hand with a denser thread across the warp. Each design is built pick by pick, demanding precision, patience and the skill of highly trained artisans."

— Rikki Kher, founder, KARDO, via IndulgeExpress

Kher named the weavers behind the cloth — Netai Mana and Brojokishore Maity — and said the recognition belonged to them. "I'm more happy for the weavers to get recognition for their craft and the team who worked tirelessly to make the piece," he told IndulgeExpress. Kate wore a pale green double-breasted blazer over a white top, with white trousers and a slim tan belt, according to IndulgeExpress. Before the cricket, the couple shared kulhad chai with Tendulkar, ANI reported.

Why they are in India

The visit is centred on the environment. "Catherine and I are delighted to be in India for this year's Earthshot Prize," the couple said in a message shared on the official Prince and Princess of Wales Instagram account, adding that India has made an extraordinary contribution to the Earthshot initiative over the past six years and is home to more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country, ANI reported. The Earthshot Prize Awards are being held in Mumbai, with two Indian finalists among those chasing the £1 million prizes — see our coverage of the Mumbai awards and the Indian finalists.

According to the British High Commission, cited by ANI, the couple will attend the 2026 Earthshot Prize ceremony and take part in engagements on climate action, sustainability, innovation and youth leadership, including India's work on sustainable transport, clean energy and responsible manufacturing. The programme also highlights cultural ties between India and the United Kingdom, including cricket, fashion and cinema. This is the couple's second official visit to India; their previous joint visit, to India and Bhutan, was in 2016, ANI reported.

What's next

After their Mumbai engagements, William and Kate travel to New Delhi to conclude the visit with a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to both IndulgeExpress and ANI. The jacket, meanwhile, has already done its work: a royal first appearance that pointed the cameras at two named weavers in a West Bengal village, rather than at a luxury label.
nri_angle: A royal visit opening in Mumbai with Indian handloom, gully cricket and the Earthshot Prize speaks directly to the UK-India cultural ties the diaspora lives between.
author: Diaspora Desk
